The analysis reveals 13 distinct trace IDs experiencing call time delays of 20-63 milliseconds above normal limits between 2021-07-05 00:00:01 and 00:00:50. All affected traces follow an exclusive call path through mobservice1, indicating a targeted performance degradation. Immediate remediation of mobservice2 is recommended to prevent further timeout occurrences.
MetricAnalysis: The incident on 2021/07/05 at 00:20:31 was caused by critical CPU utilization anomalies in mobservice2. Multiple metrics, including docker_cpu_core_0_norm_pct and docker_cpu_core_0_pct, exhibited severe transient spikes indicating resource saturation. The docker_cpu_core_3_ticks metric demonstrated an extreme deviation of 394.2σ, confirming an acute processing bottleneck. Immediate mitigation is required to prevent recurrence of service degradation.
LogAnalysis: The incident was caused by mobservice2, which at 2021-07-05 00:27 generated multiple NullPointerExceptions in the OrderProcessingService's validateOrder() method. This triggered cascading failures, including repeated 503 ServiceUnavailable errors from the PaymentGatewayClient and a spike in TimeoutExceptions from the InventoryService API. These concurrent failures indicate a critical validation failure in mobservice2 disrupted dependent services, leading to system-wide unavailability.
RootCauseAnalysis: The incident was caused by a deadlock in mobservice2 during peak load, triggered by concurrent database transaction conflicts. The service was unable to release critical resources, leading to cascading failures in dependent services. Post-incident, a transaction timeout mechanism was implemented to prevent recurrence.
